- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile; use 3-day moving average or median of recent 5-day window to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; add 1–2% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values followed by a spike, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true breakout.
